## Sharper population for the body's count — the union's arms, not a hand-picked set of interfaces

Raised as finding F1 by the independent review of PR #9548, and **re-measured in this seat rather
than adopted**: `origin/main` = `b7479abc74100e022b5f1233fd14d4fabc891788`, `2026-09-15T03:05Z`.

The body counts "eleven node schemas declared in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, of which the
barrel carries ten". That population is a set of interfaces I enumerated by eye. ⭐ The principled
population is the one the type system itself names — the arms of
`export type ObjectQLComponentSchema`, the type that says what an ObjectQL node may be:

```
ObjectGridSchema · ObjectFormSchema · ObjectViewSchema · ObjectMapSchema · ObjectTreeSchema
ObjectGanttSchema · ObjectCalendarSchema · ObjectKanbanSchema · ObjectChartSchema
ObjectGallerySchema · ObjectDataTableSchema · ListViewSchema
```

**12 arms. 11 are named by `packages/types/src/index.ts`. Exactly one is not: `ObjectTreeSchema`**
(occurrence count in that file, per arm: 2 · 2 · 2 · 1 · **0** · 1 · 1 · 2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 3).
Absent-token control in the same file: 0.

⇒ the two arms my first count had left out — `ListViewSchema` and `ObjectViewSchema` — are **both**
exported, so the finding survives the wider population and gets stronger: it is not "ten of eleven
by one reading", it is **one arm of twelve, and only one**, missing from the barrel that publishes
the union.

⛔ Nothing in the body is false; it is just measured over a population I chose instead of one the
code declares. ⭐ The lesson is the one this lane keeps paying for: **the population you choose
defines the defects you cannot find** — and when a type already declares the population, using a
hand-rolled one is choosing to be less checkable for no gain.

Whoever grades or repairs this should quote the 12 / 11 / 1 reading.

The triage grading on this card ([`5710385032`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/9550#issuecomment-5710385032)) ends its 修法边界 section with, verbatim:

**This seat's dispatch order did not carry that line.** It went further in the wrong direction: it wrote a Zone 1 ruling reading "the ask is the ONE name" and put `packages/plugin-tree` behind an explicit fence. ⇒ the implementer was ⛔ **not** permitted to do the thing the card's own ruling asked for, and it behaved **correctly** against the order it was given — it measured the site, declined to touch it, and reported it as out of scope in as many words. ⭐ The narrowing is mine.

### Why the reviewer is right on the merits, not merely on the letter

The grading's whole p2 rationale is that the missing export **mints a fresh second authority every time someone needs the type** — it is one item of the objectui#6349 burn-down (29 remaining on triage's last count). ⇒ exporting the name while leaving the hand-copy in place fixes the *mechanism* and leaves the *instance*, and closes the card. That is precisely the failure the ruling's last clause names: 「这张卡看起来已经修好了」.

### The patch round — one item

Per the record's Blocking 1, in **this** PR:

1. In `packages/plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx`: replace the module-local `Extract` alias with a type-only named import of `ObjectTreeSchema` from `@object-ui/types`; use it at both read sites (`ObjectTreeProps.schema` and `getTreeConfig`'s parameter).
2. Delete the now-false justification paragraph (the one whose measured reason is that the name cannot be imported). ⛔ **Keep** the second paragraph — the shadowing warning citing objectui#8651. It stays true and gets *more* load-bearing once the published name is importable.
3. Add a `'@object-ui/plugin-tree': patch` changeset. ⛔ Never `major`.
4. Re-run `ObjectTree.schemaTyped-8655.test.ts` (row 20 of the record: it does not pin the idiom, so it should stay green) and that package's `type-check`.

⭐ The prerequisites are already measured, so this is not a fishing trip: `packages/plugin-tree/src` is disjoint from **all 13** open PRs (record row 16), and the imported type is provably equal to the `Extract` spelling (record row 9, assertion `a2`).

### Consequences this seat is handling, ⛔ not leaving to the dev

- **objectui#9687** — this seat filed that card ~40 minutes ago for exactly this repair, on the assumption the fence was correct. With the repair moving back into this PR, that card is **superseded**; this seat will close it as a duplicate once the patch lands, so nobody picks it up in parallel.
- **The file fence in the claim comment is hereby amended** to include `packages/plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx` and a `plugin-tree` changeset. ⛔ The rest of the fence stands — `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and `zod/objectql.zod.ts` remain frozen behind PR #9540.
